alt.en: One line of old printed music on cream paper, headed "ROW, ROW. Round.", in 6/8 with two sharps, the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4 printed over it every two bars. The words under it read "Row, row, row your boat, Gently down the stream; Merrily, merrily, merrily, merrily; Life is but a dream."
alt.es: Una línea de música impresa antigua sobre papel color crema, con el título "ROW, ROW. Round.", en 6/8 con dos sostenidos, y los números 1, 2, 3 y 4 impresos encima cada dos compases. La letra debajo dice "Row, row, row your boat, Gently down the stream; Merrily, merrily, merrily, merrily; Life is but a dream."

caption.en: "Row, Row. Round." on page 39 of The Teachers' Institute Glee Book (Lancaster, Pa., 1874), prepared by W. B. Hall and E. O. Lyte: the round's earliest known printing, with no name beside it and the numbers 1 to 4 marking where each voice comes in.
caption.es: "Row, Row. Round." en la página 39 de The Teachers' Institute Glee Book (Lancaster, Pensilvania, 1874), preparado por W. B. Hall y E. O. Lyte: la primera impresión conocida del canon, sin ningún nombre al lado y con los números del 1 al 4 donde entra cada voz.

source: W. B. Hall and E. O. Lyte, preparers, The Teachers' Institute Glee Book (Lancaster, Pa.: Hall & Lyte, 1874), p. 39, "Row, Row. Round." (image n40); cropped to the round, leaving out the end of Lightly Row above it and God Speed the Right below it
library: Music Library, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (Internet Archive)
callNumber: b76447923; Internet Archive teachersinstitut00hall, image n40
licenceEvidence: Printed 1874; the round is unsigned here, its tune credited to E. O. Lyte (died 1913) from 1881, its words traditional. The crop holds only the round. IA metadata has no rights field; PD-old by age. See rights.md.
credit: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Music Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: Two lines of old printed music headed "No. 5. ROW, ROW. Round.", signed "E. O. L." and marked "From "The School Song Book."", with the numbers 1 to 4 over the staves. The words read "Row, row, row your boat, Gen-tly down the stream; Mer-ri-ly, mer-ri-ly, mer-ri-ly, mer-ri-ly; Life is but a dream."
alt.es: Dos líneas de música impresa antigua con el título "No. 5. ROW, ROW. Round.", firmadas "E. O. L." y con la nota "From "The School Song Book."", y los números del 1 al 4 sobre los pentagramas. La letra dice "Row, row, row your boat, Gen-tly down the stream; Mer-ri-ly, mer-ri-ly, mer-ri-ly, mer-ri-ly; Life is but a dream."

caption.en: No. 5 of E. O. Lyte's own The School Bell (Lancaster, Pa., 1893), signed with his initials "E. O. L.": the printing our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: El n.º 5 de The School Bell (Lancaster, Pensilvania, 1893), el propio libro de E. O. Lyte, firmado con sus iniciales "E. O. L.": la impresión de la que está leído nuestro arreglo.

source: E. Oram Lyte, The School Bell: 150 Songs and Hymns Adapted to the Use of Schools (Lancaster, Pa.: Manor Publishing Company, 1893; copyright 1892 by E. Oram Lyte), No. 5, "Row, Row. Round." (image n7); cropped to No. 5, leaving out No. 4, Night, above it
library: Music Library, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (Internet Archive)
callNumber: b78151922; Internet Archive schoolbell150son00lyte, image n7
licenceEvidence: Printed 1893 (copyright 1892); author and publisher of the book E. Oram Lyte, died 1913; the crop holds only his signed round. IA metadata has no rights field; PD-old by age. See rights.md.
credit: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Music Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A black-and-white photograph of a large four-storey school building with a shingled mansard roof, corner turrets and three storeys of long wooden porches with railings, beside a brick tower with arched windows. Bare trees stand on the lawn in front, and paved paths curve across the grass.
alt.es: Una fotografía en blanco y negro de un gran edificio escolar de cuatro plantas, con tejado abuhardillado de tejas de madera, torrecillas en las esquinas y tres plantas de largos porches de madera con barandillas, junto a una torre de ladrillo con ventanas en arco. Delante, en el césped, hay árboles sin hojas, y caminos pavimentados cruzan la hierba en curva.

caption.en: The State Normal School at Millersville, Pennsylvania, photographed in 1921: E. O. Lyte studied and taught at the school and was its principal from 1887 to 1912.
caption.es: La escuela normal del estado en Millersville, Pensilvania, fotografiada en 1921: E. O. Lyte estudió y enseñó en la escuela y fue su director de 1887 a 1912.

source: Millersville State Normal School, Millersville, Pa., panoramic photograph, gelatin silver print, c1921 Darmstaetter's (Lancaster, Pa.); cropped to the main building and tower, about a third of the panorama

alt.en: A printed page numbered 224 with three short verses: "Children yet, the tale to hear, Eager eye and willing ear, Lovingly shall nestle near. In a Wonderland they lie, Dreaming as the days go by, Dreaming as the summers die: Ever drifting down the stream, Lingering in the golden gleam, Life, what is it but a dream?" Below them: "THE END."
alt.es: Una página impresa con el número 224 y tres estrofas breves: "Children yet, the tale to hear, Eager eye and willing ear, Lovingly shall nestle near. In a Wonderland they lie, Dreaming as the days go by, Dreaming as the summers die: Ever drifting down the stream, Lingering in the golden gleam, Life, what is it but a dream?" Debajo: "THE END."

caption.en: The last page of Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass (London, dated 1872), whose closing poem ends "Life, what is it but a dream?": the same old thought as the round's last line, though no source we found links the two.
caption.es: La última página de Through the Looking-Glass, de Lewis Carroll (Londres, fechado en 1872), cuyo poema final termina con "Life, what is it but a dream?" (la vida, ¿qué es sino un sueño?): la misma vieja idea que el último verso del canon, aunque ninguna fuente que encontramos relaciona los dos.

source: Lewis Carroll, Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There (London: Macmillan and Co., 1872), p. 224, the end of the closing poem; the page as printed, its margins trimmed
callNumber: Riess C319T; Internet Archive throughlookinggl01carr, p. 224
licenceEvidence: Title page dated 1872 (Macmillan, London); author Lewis Carroll (C. L. Dodgson) died 1898; the page has no illustration. IA metadata has no rights field; PD-old by age. See rights.md.
